sections.title: All things are vanity because of their nature.

verses.text: በኢየሩሳሌም ለእስራኤል የነገሠ የዳዊት ልጅ የሰባኪው የሰሎሞን ቃል።
ሰባኪው፥ “ከንቱ፥ ከንቱ፥ የከንቱ ከንቱ ሁሉ ከንቱ ነው” ይላል።
ከፀሐይ በታች በሚደክምበት ድካም ሁሉ የሰው ትርፉ ምንድን ነው?
ትውልድ ያልፋል፥ ትውልድም ይመጣል፤ ምድር ግን ለዘለዓለም ጸንታ ትኖራለች።
ፀሐይ ይወጣል፥ ፀሐይም ይገባል፥ ወደሚወጣበትም ስፍራ ይመለሳል፤
ወደ ቀኝ ይመለሳል፥ ወደ ሰሜንም ይዞራል፤ ነፋስ ዙሪያዉን ዙሮ ይሄዳል፥ ነፋስም በዙረቱ ይመለሳል።
ፈሳሾች ሁሉ ወደ ባሕር ይሄዳሉ፥ ባሕሩ ግን አይሞላም፤ ፈሳሾች ወደሚሄዱበት ስፍራ እንደ ገና ወደዚያ ይመለሳሉ።
ነገር ሁሉ ያደክማል፤ ሰውም ይናገረው ዘንድ አይችልም፥ ዐይን በማየት አይጠግብም፥ ጆሮም በመስማት አይሞላም።
የሆነው ነገር እርሱ የሚሆን ነው፥ የተደረገውም ነገር እርሱ የሚደረግ ነው፥ ከፀሐይም በታች ከተደረገው ሁሉ አዲስ ነገር የለም።
እነሆ፥ “ይህ ነገር አዲስ ነው” ብሎ የሚናገር ማን ነው? እርሱ ከእኛ በፊት በነበሩት ዘመናት ተደርጓል።
There is no remembrance for those who go before; nor is there any remembrance for those who come after among those who will arise.
I was a king over Israel in Jerusalem.
I set my heart to seek and to search out by wisdom concerning all that is done under heaven; this sore travail hath God given to the sons of men to be exercised therewith.
I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and behold, all is vanity and a striving after wind.
A generation goes, and a generation comes; but the earth abides forever.
I said in my heart, “Behold, I have increased in wisdom more than all that were before me in Jerusalem; my heart also has had great experience of wisdom and knowledge.”
My heart has pondered much wisdom and knowledge; I have considered the task of gathering wisdom, and it is like a striving after wind.
For in much wisdom is much grief, and he who increases knowledge increases sorrow.
እኔ በልቤ፥ “ና በደስታም እፈትንሃለሁ፥ እነሆ፥ መልካምንም እይ” አልሁ፤ ይህም እነሆ፥ ከንቱ ነበረ።
ሣቅን፥ “ሽንገላ ነህ፤ ደስታንም፦ ምን ታደርጋለህ?” አልሁት።
የሰው ልጆች በሕይወታቸው ዘመን ሁሉ ከፀሐይ በታች የሚሠሩት መልካም ነገር ምን እንደ ሆነ እስካይ ድረስ ልቤ በጥበብ እየመራኝ፥ ሰውነቴን በወይን ደስ ለማሰኘት፥ ስንፍናንም ለመያዝ በልቤ መረመርሁ።
እኔ ሥራዬን አበዛሁ፥ ቤቶችንም ለእኔ ሠራሁ፥ ወይንም ተከልሁ።
የወይንና የአትክልት ቦታን አደረግሁ፥ ወይንና ልዩ ልዩ ፍሬ ያለባቸውንም ዛፎች ተከልሁባቸው።
የሚያፈራ እንጨትንና የተተከሉትን ዛፎች አጠጣበት ዘንድ የውኃ ማጠራቀሚያን አደረግሁ።
ወንዶችና ሴቶች አገልጋዮችን ገዛሁ፤ በቤት የተወለዱ አገልጋዮችም ነበሩኝ፤ ከእኔ አስቀድመው በኢየሩሳሌም ከነበሩት ሁሉ ይልቅ ብዙ የበጎችና የከብቶች መንጋዎች ነበሩኝ።
ብርንና ወርቅን፥ የከበረውንም የነገሥታትንና የአውራጆችን መዝገብ ለራሴ ሰበሰብሁ፤ ሴቶችና ወንዶች አዝማሪዎችን፥ የሰዎች ልጆችንም ተድላ አደረግሁ፤ የወይን ጠጅ ጠማቂዎችንና አሳላፊዎችንም አበዛሁ።
ከእኔም አስቀድመው በኢየሩሳሌም ከነበሩት ሁሉ ይልቅ ከበርሁ፥ ታላቅም ሆንሁ። ጥበቤም ከእኔ ጋር ጸናችልኝ።
ዐይኖቼ ከፈለጉት ሁሉ አላጣሁም፥ ልቤንም ከደስታ ሁሉ አልከለከልሁትም፤ ልቤ በድካሜ ሁሉ ደስ ይለው ነበርና፤ ከድካሜም ሁሉ ይህ ዕድል ፋንታዬ ሆነ።
I have considered all my works, and all my labors wherein I have toiled; behold, all is vanity, and a striving after wind, and there is no profit under the sun.
I have also considered wisdom, and madness, and folly; for what can the man do who comes after the king? Only that which has already been done.
I have also seen that the light excels the darkness, and that the wise man's eyes are in his head, but the fool walks in darkness; and I perceived that the same event happens to them all.
The wise man's eyes are in his head, but the fool walks in darkness; and I have also seen that one event happens to them all.
I said in my heart, "As it happens to the fool, so it will happen to me also; and why then should I be more wise?" And I said in my heart that this also is vanity.
For there is no remembrance of the wise more than of the fool forever; seeing that which now is in the days to come shall all be forgotten; and how dies the wise man? As the fool dies!
All the works that are done under the sun are vanity and a striving after wind; for I have seen that all is vanity and a striving after wind.
I hated all my labor which I had taken under the sun, because I should leave it unto the man that shall be after me.
For what is man, that he should be wise or foolish, under the sun? In all my labor wherein I have labored under the sun, I have seen that this also is vanity.
I turned to consider my heart, and I gave up all hope concerning all my labor which I had taken under the sun.
A man, after he has fallen into weakness through wisdom and knowledge, shall pass his fortune to another who has not fallen; this also is a great vanity and a grievous affliction.
Under the sun, in the time of his affliction, it is not good for man to have all thoughts in his heart;
All the days of his life are affliction, and sorrow, and vexation; his heart also does not rest by night; this too is vanity.
For man, apart from eating and drinking, there is nothing good that he can show for his body when he is weary; there is no good thing, except that which is given as a gift from the hand of God.
Who is he that eats or drinks without his permission?

He shall grant wisdom and knowledge, and joy to the man who is good in His sight; but to the sinner, He shall give the task of gathering and collecting, that he may give to him who is good before God. This also is vanity, and a striving after wind.

sections.title: There is a time for everything.

verses.text: To everything there is a season, and a time for every matter under heaven.
A time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up what is planted;
A time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a time to build up;
A time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;
A time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;
A time to seek, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away;
A time to rend, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak;
A time to love, and a time to hate; a time for war, and a time for peace.
What is the profit to the laborer from his toil?
The Lord has given to man the burden of labor, and I cannot bear all the toil that He has given them.
All that He has made is beautiful in its time; God has also set eternity in the hearts of men, yet they cannot fathom what God has done from beginning to end.
I have observed that there is nothing better for a man than to rejoice and to do good while he lives; and that there is no good thing in him apart from the good he does.
Moreover, all men eat and drink, and find satisfaction in all their toil; this is the gift of God.
I know that whatever God does endures forever; nothing can be added to it, and nothing taken from it. God has done this so that men may fear before Him.
What has been is what will be, and what has been done is what will be done; and there is nothing new under the sun. God will bring back what is past.
I have seen that under the sun, in the place of righteousness there is wickedness, and in the place of justice there is wickedness.
In my heart, I said, “For everything there is a season, and for every matter under heaven, God will judge both the righteous and the wicked.”
I said in my heart regarding the children of men, “God will judge them, so that they may see that they are like the animals.”

For the children of men, death is their fate; for the animals, death is their fate; one fate awaits them both; as one dies, so dies the other; all have the same breath; man has no advantage over the animals; all is vanity.
All go to one place; all come from dust, and to dust all return.
Who knows the soul of man, that it ascends on high, and the soul of the beast, that it descends downward to the earth?
For this is the chance of the fate; I have seen that there is no good thing besides the joy of a man in his labor; who can bring him to see what shall be after him?

And I returned, and beneath the sun I beheld all the oppression that is done; and behold, the oppressed had no comforter, and power was on the side of their oppressors. Yet, there was no comforter for them.
And I say, even to this day, I have more reason to commend the dead who have died in times past than the living who are yet alive.
Better is he who has not yet been born than both of these, for he has not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.

I have seen all the oppressions that are done under the sun, and behold, the tears of the oppressed; and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors was power, but they had no comforter.
He will stretch forth his hands to eat, and he will consume his own flesh.
Better is one hand full of rest than two hands full of labor and striving after the wind.
And I returned, and beneath the sun I beheld vanity.

There is one alone, and there is not a second; he has neither child nor brother; yet there is no end to all his labor; and his eyes are not satisfied with riches. For whom then do I labor, and bereave my soul of good? This also is vanity, and a grievous task.
For their strength is a good reward, and it is better to have two than to be alone.
If one falls, the other will lift him up; but woe to him who is alone when he falls, for there is not another to lift him up.
If two lie together, they will keep warm; but how can one be warm alone?
If one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
It is better for a poor and wise child than for an old and foolish king who will no more be admonished.
Though he be a debtor to the king, he hath gone out of the house of bondage to the king.
Under the sun, I have seen all the living who walk with the youth, and I have seen them together with another.
The people who were before him had no number; but they that come after shall not rejoice in him. This also is vanity, and a striving after wind.
When thou goest to the house of God, keep thy foot; and draw near to hear the instruction of the wise, and be not hasty to offer the sacrifice of fools; for they know not that they do evil.
God is in heaven, and thou art upon the earth; therefore let thy words be few. For a dream cometh through the multitude of business, and a fool's voice is known by multitude of words.
For in the multitude of dreams and many words there are also divers vanities; but fear thou God.
If thou vow a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for He hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed. Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.
Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel that it was an error: wherefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thine hands?
For in the multitude of dreams and many words there are also divers vanities; but fear thou God.
For in the multitude of dreams, and in many words, there is also vanity; but fear thou God.

For he who is high above shall keep watch over you, and others shall rise above them; when the poor in your land are oppressed, and justice and righteousness are trampled upon, do not let your work be in vain.
The benefit of the earth is for all, and the benefit of the king is in the field.
A man who loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver; likewise, he who loves abundance shall not be satisfied. This is also vanity.
When wealth increases, those who consume it shall increase; apart from what the eye can see, what benefit is there to its owner?
Whether one eats much or little, the sleep of the servant is sweet; but he who increases his labor shall not find rest.
I have seen a grievous evil under the sun; it is a burden to its owner.
This burden shall perish in wickedness; even if a child is born, there is nothing in his hand.
As he came forth from his mother's womb, so shall he return; and from his toil, he shall carry nothing away.
This too is a grievous evil; as he came, so shall he go. What then is the profit for the one who toils for his own body?
All the days of his life are spent in darkness, in sorrow, and in much vexation, in grief and in anguish.

Behold, I have seen that which is good and pleasing: man shall eat and drink in the days of his life which God hath given him under the sun, and in every toil wherein he labors, this is the portion of his lot.
The Lord bestows upon every man both wealth and abundance, that he may eat thereof and receive his portion in joy; even in his toil, this is the gift of God.
The Lord, for the joy that is in his heart, doth not consider the days of his life at all.
ከፀሐይ በታች ያየሁት ክፉ ነገር አለ፥ እርሱም በሰው ላይ እጅግ የበዛ ነው።
እግዚአብሔር ለሰው ሀብትንና ጥሪትን ክብርንም ሰጠው፥ ከወደደውም ሁሉ ለሰውነቱ የከለከላት የለም፤ ነገር ግን ሌላ ሰው ይበላዋል እንጂ ከእርሱ ይበላ ዘንድ እግዚአብሔር አላሠለጠነውም፤ ይህም ከንቱና ክፉ ደዌ ነው።
ሰው መቶ ልጆች ቢወልድ፥ ብዙ ዘመንም በሕይወት ቢኖር፥ ዕድሜውም ብዙ ዓመት ቢሆን፥ ነገር ግን ነፍሱ መልካምን ባትጠግብ፥ መቃብርንም ባያገኝ፥ እኔ ስለ እርሱ፥ “ከእርሱ ይልቅ ጭንጋፍ ይሻላል” አልሁ።
በከንቱ መጥቶአል፥ በጨለማም ይሄዳል፥ ስሙ በጨለማ ይሸፈናልና።
ደግሞም ፀሐይን አላየም፥ አላወቀምም፤ ስለዚህ ከዚያ ይልቅ ለዚህ ዕረፍት አለው።
ሺህ ዓመት ሁለት ጊዜ በሕይወት ቢኖር፥ መልካምንም ባያይ፥ ሁሉ ወደ አንድ ስፍራ የሚሄድ አይደለምን?
የሰው ድካም ሁሉ በአፉ ነው፥ ነፍሱ ግን አትጠግብም።
ከአላዋቂ ይልቅ ለጠቢብ ጥቅሙ ምንድር ነው? በሕያዋን ፊትስ መሄድን ለሚያውቅ ለድሃ ጥቅሙ ምንድር ነው?
በዐይን ማየት በነፍስ ከመቅበዝበዝ ይሻላል፥ ይህ ደግሞ ከንቱ ነው፥ ነፋስንም እንደ መከተል ነው።
የሆነው ሁሉ እነሆ፥ ስሙ አስቀድሞ ተጠራ፥ ሰውም እንደ ሆነ ታወቀ፤ ከእርሱም ከሚበረታው ጋር ይፋረድ ዘንድ አይችልም።
For there are many things that are vanity; what is the worth of man?
Who knows what is good for man during the few days of his vain life, which he spends like a shadow? Or who can tell man what shall be after him under the sun?
A good name is better than precious ointment, and the day of death is better than the day of one's birth.
It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting; for that is the end of all men, and the living will lay it to heart.
It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting; for sorrow is better than laughter, for by the sadness of the countenance the heart is made better.
The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.
It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise than for a man to hear the song of fools.
For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool; this also is vanity.
Oppression makes a wise man mad, and a gift destroys the heart.
Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof; and the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.
Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry, for anger resteth in the bosom of fools.
Say not thou, What is the cause that the former days were better than these? For thou dost not inquire wisely concerning this.
ጥበብ ከርስት ጋር መልካም ነው፤ ፀሓይንም ለሚያዩ ሰዎች ትርፍን ይሰጣል።
የጥበብ ጥላ ከብር ጥላ ይሻላል፤ የጥበብንም ዕውቀት ማብዛት ገንዘብ ላደረጋት ሕይወትን ትሰጠዋለች።
የእግዚአብሔርን ሥራ ተመልከት፤ እግዚአብሔር ጠማማ ያደረገውን ማን ሊያቀናው ይችላል?
በመልካም ቀን ደስ ይበልህ ፤ በክፉም ቀን ተመልከት፤ ሰው ከእርሱ በኋላ መርምሮ ምንም እንዳያገኝ እግዚአብሔር ይህንም ያንም እንደዚያ ሠራ።
ጻድቅ በጽድቁ ሲጠፋ፥ ኃጥእም በክፋቱ ሲኖር፥ ይህን ሁሉ በከንቱ ዘመኔ አየሁ።
እጅግ ጻድቅ አትሁን፥ እጅግም ጠቢብ አትሁን፥ እንዳትበድል።
እጅግ ክፉ አትሁን፥ እልከኛም አትሁን፥ ያለ ጊዜህ እንዳትሞት።
ይህን ብትይዝ ለአንተ መልካም ነው፤ በዚህም እጅህን አታርክስ፥ እግዚአብሔርን የሚፈራ ከሁሉ ይወጣልና።
በከተማ ከሚኖሩ ዐሥር ገዢዎች ይልቅ ጥበብ ጠቢብን ትረዳዋለች።
በምድር ላይም መልካምን የሚሠራ ኀጢአትንም የማያደርግ ጻድቅ ሰው አይገኝምና።
When thy servant calleth upon thee, let not thy heart be troubled by every word that is spoken in jest.
For he hath often deceived thee; and in many ways hath thy heart been led astray, and thou too art known to others as one who is deceived.
All these things I have tested with wisdom; I have said, I will be wise, but it is far from me.
Who is it that can find a thing that is far off and exceedingly hidden?
I seek wisdom and the gathering of all that hath been spoken; I desire to understand the ways of the wicked and the paths of the deceitful, for my heart is heavy within me.
I have found a thing more bitter than death; it is a woman whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands are bands; whosoever pleaseth God shall escape from her, but the sinner shall be taken by her.
Behold, the seeker saith, I have found this matter; I have added one to another to understand all that hath been spoken.
My soul hath not found what it seeketh; among thousands of men I have found one, but among all these I have not found a single woman.
The Lord hath made men upright; but they have sought out many inventions; behold, I have found this alone, yet they have sought much knowledge.

sections.title: Concerning the honor of the king.

verses.text: Who knows the thoughts of the wise? And who is able to interpret their words? The wisdom of man is like a light that shines forth; but a man without understanding shall be cast away.
My son, keep the words of the king; do not forsake the command of your mother.
For he shall do all that he desires; depart from his presence, and do not stand in the way of evil.
The king has power according to his station; why then do you act thus? Who will question him?
He who keeps the commandment knows not evil; the heart of the wise discerns the time for judgment.
The knowledge of man is great, for in him there is time and judgment for all matters.
Yet there is none who knows what shall be; who can declare how it shall come to pass?
There is no man who has power over the spirit to retain it; nor is there power in the day of death; and in the time of war, there is no refuge; neither shall sin deliver its maker.
I have seen all this in unity; under the sun, I have given my heart to all the work that is done; for there is a time when man shall rise against man to be a ruler.

sections.title: The condition of the wicked and the righteous.

verses.text: And likewise, at that time, the wicked entered into the strong grave, and they departed from the holy place; and they were gathered in the city, saying, "Thus have they served us," and this is also in vain.
There is no one who hastens to do evil and causes strife; therefore, the hearts of the children of men are inclined to do evil.
From ancient times, they have committed sin, and I know that for those who fear God, it shall be for their safety before Him.
But for the wicked, there is no safety; they do not fear before God, and their time shall not be like a shadow.
There is a vain thing done under the sun; the work done by the wicked shall reach the righteous, and the work done for the righteous shall reach the wicked; this also is in vain, I say.
Aside from what is eaten and drunk, there is no good thing under the sun for man; therefore, I give thanks for joy; this is what God has given him in his lifetime.
Know wisdom, for it is not the weariness that is in the earth; I have given my heart to it, for there is no sleep in the day or the night that my eyes can see.

Consider the work done under the sun, for it is not possible for man to attain all the work of God; even if a man strives greatly, he shall not attain it; and likewise, a wise man, if he says, "I know this," he shall not be able to attain it.

I have given my heart to all this in unity; the works of the righteous and the wise are in the hand of God. My heart has regarded all this; whether it be love or hatred, man knows not; all is before them.

There is vanity in all, of the righteous and the wicked, of the good and the evil, of the clean and the unclean, of him who offers a sacrifice and him who does not offer, of the good and likewise of the sinner, of the one who swears and likewise of the one who fears an oath; one portion is for all.

All that is done under the sun is evil for all; for the portion of all is one. Moreover, the hearts of the children of men are full of evil; while they live, their hearts are afflicted, and afterward they descend to the dead.
Whosoever is in unity with the living has hope; for a living dog is better than a dead lion.
They know how to die, but the dead know nothing; neither do they have any more a reward; for the memory of them is forgotten, and after this, they have no worth.
Their love and their hatred, their envy, behold, they have perished; and under the sun, in all that is done, there is no longer any portion for them forever.
The Lord has accepted your work; therefore, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a merry heart; for God has already approved your deeds.
Always let your garments be white; and let not oil be lacking upon your head.
In your life, if you are under the sun and you are in sorrow, this is your portion; in all the days of your life, under the sun, in the vain days you have, may joy be with your wife whom you love.
In the place you go, in Sheol, there is no work or thought; knowledge and wisdom are not found there; therefore, do all that your hand finds to do, according to your strength.

And I returned, beneath the sun, running for the swift, war for the mighty, bread for the wise, and wealth for the prudent; yet I saw that wisdom is not for the wise, for time and chance happen to them all.
A man does not know his time; as the fish are caught in an evil net, and as the birds are taken in a snare, so are the sons of men ensnared in an evil time when it falls suddenly upon them.
Beneath the sun, I have seen wisdom, and it is great in my sight.
There was a small city, and few men were in it; and a great king came against it and besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it.
A wise but poor man was found in it, and by his wisdom he delivered the city; yet no one remembered that poor man.
And I said, “Wisdom is better than strength; but the wisdom of the poor man is despised, and his words are not heard.”
The words of the wise are heard in quiet more than the cry of him that rules among fools.
Wisdom is better than weapons of war; but one sinner destroys much good.
The sting of death has seized the olive oil; rather than great honor, it is the small wisdom that prevails in the midst of affliction.
The heart of the wise is on the right side, but the heart of the foolish is on the left side.
Moreover, when folly takes hold of the heart, and the path it walks upon, the mind shall be led astray; all that it contemplates is indeed folly.
For wisdom shall deliver the great sin, and when the wrath of the ruler rises against you, do not forsake your place.
There is a wicked thing that I have seen under the sun; it is an error that proceeds from the ruler who knows not.
Folly is set upon a great throne, but the wise sit in a lowly place.
As servants sit upon horses, so have I seen princes walking upon the earth as servants.
He who digs a pit for his neighbor shall fall into it; and he who breaks down a wall, a serpent shall bite him.
He who breaks a stone shall be hurt by it; and he who splits wood shall be endangered by it.
If the serpent bites before it is charmed, then the biter is without remedy; much strength is required. But wisdom is the profit of the strong man.
If a serpent strikes, though there be a healer, the healer shall not avail; for he shall not be of use.
The words of a wise man are as a sweet savor; but the foolish shall bring forth their own destruction.
The beginning of the words is folly, and the end of the discourse is evil.
The foolish shall abound in words; and a man shall not know what is to come; who shall declare what shall be after him?
The foolish are burdened with their own troubles, and they know not how to go to the city.
Your king is a child; and your nobles shall feed on the weak; O land, woe unto you!
Your king is the son of the Lord; and your nobles shall feed on the weak in due season, and they shall not fear; O land, you are blessed!
In the folly of men, the threshold of the house shall be broken; and in the hands of the foolish, the house shall be brought low.
The foolish shall prepare bread for the hungry; and the wine shall bring joy to the living; all shall be bought for money.

For the birds of heaven shall carry forth your words; and the thing that has wings shall declare your matters; even if your thoughts be in your heart, do not trouble the king; and in your house of rest, do not trouble the master.

sections.title: For that which is fitting to be done wisely.

verses.text: He has cast your bread upon the waters; after many days you shall find it again.
For seven, and likewise for eight, do not give your heart to the evil that is done under the sun, for you do not know what will happen.
When the clouds are full, they empty themselves upon the earth; and if a tree falls to the south or to the north, in the place where the tree falls, there it shall lie.
The wind does not know its way, nor does it regard the clouds.
Just as you do not know the way of the wind, or how the bones grow in the womb of her who is with child, so you do not know the work of God who makes everything.
This or that, whichever it may be, do not know whether it is good or both are good, and in the morning sow your seed, and in the evening do not let your hand be idle.
Light is sweet, and it is pleasant for the eyes to behold the sun.
Though a man may live many years and rejoice in them all, let him remember the days of darkness, for they will be many; all that is coming is vanity.

Thou art blessed; may joy be upon thee in thy blessedness, and may thy heart rejoice in thy blessedness, and in the way of thy heart, may thy eyes go forth to behold; yet for this matter, may the Lord bring thee unto judgment.
Childhood and blessedness, being unaware, are indeed vanity; therefore, cast away thy wrath from thy heart, and remove evil from thy body.
Before the day of distress comes, remember your Creator in the days of your youth; rejoice not in the years that come upon you, which shall not bring you joy.
The sun and the light, the moon and the stars shall not be darkened, and the clouds shall not return after the rain.

In the place where the watchmen are appointed, and the mighty men gather, there are few, and the works of the diligent are sought; whether through the window or through the doors, they shall be observed when they are opened.
On the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows be darkened;

When they look up to the high places, and the almond tree shall flourish, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail; for man goeth to his long home, and the mourners go about the streets;

The silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern; and the dust return to the earth as it was, and the spirit return unto God who gave it.

Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the days come when you shall say, “I have no pleasure in them,” before the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars be darkened, and the clouds return after the rain.
The preacher said, “Vanity of vanities; all is vanity.”
And the preacher, being wise, taught the people knowledge; yea, he gave good heed, and sought out, and set in order many proverbs.
The preacher sought to find out acceptable words; and that which was written was upright, even words of truth.
The words of the wise are as a refuge for the strong; and the words that are gathered from one who is diligent are as treasures that have been hidden.
Above all these, my son, heed my instruction; do not neglect the many writings that lack conclusion. Indeed, much inquiry brings weariness to the flesh.
Hear the conclusion of all that has been spoken; for this is the whole duty of man: Fear God and keep His commandments.
The Lord shall bring forth all that is hidden, whether it be good or evil, for He shall bring it to judgment.
